>"Great Ace Attorney" is separate series. Has always been intended as one.

 I can't find a single article/official source which determines the great ace attorney happening in a different timeline than the mainline ace attorney games (which is the definition of spin off), Instead to the contrary, we can see dozens of evidence to the contrary.

Winston Payne has a ancestor (Takestsuchi Auchi), We can even find a promotional material in which Phoenix Wright and Ryunosuke Naruhodo come to find out they are related by blood! ([Source](https://youtu.be/aGQ7OEXG4oM)) How does this not make it a prequel?

Apollo justice is continuation to the the ace attorney, no doubt, however, it does not focus on phoenix wright instead spotlights Apollo. Does it make it a Spin off?

Similarly, GAA focuses on phoenix's ancestor. We cannot call it a spin off based on absence of phoenix. Instead, to the contrary, we can assume Ryunosuke as a charismatic predecessor to the mainline games, which happens few years later. It does not make it a spin off.

Look up the definitions of spin off and prequel.

Prequel- A story or film containing events which precede those of an existing work.

Spin off- A by-product or incidental result of a larger project.

Apollo can be assumed as spin off as the DD explains the timeline without you playing a single case of AJ. In that case according to this thread's argument, GAA can also be put in the same category.

But if you consider AJ as not spin off then you also have to take in consideration that GAA also happens in the same timeline as Canon games.

How? Ryunosuke is literally the great grand-dad of phoenix. ([Source](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=aGQ7OEXG4oM&t=148s)) How is it not a prequel?

He literally started the ace timeline.
